name: Botswana
system_note: The president is elected by parliament and heads the government.
snapshot: One of Africa's most stable democracies, now led by its first opposition government and searching for a future beyond diamonds as global demand slumps.
culture: Botswana takes its name from the Tswana people, and Setswana is spoken by nearly everyone alongside English. The kgotla, a village assembly where elders and residents debate in public, is a living tradition that the state still uses for consultation. Cattle remain central to status and family wealth. The Okavango Delta and the Kalahari underpin a high-end safari industry that deliberately limits visitor numbers.
society: At independence in 1966 Botswana was among the poorest countries on Earth; diamond revenue, managed through a joint venture with De Beers, built roads, schools and clinics. The country fought one of the world's worst HIV epidemics and now has high treatment coverage. Unemployment, especially among young people, is stubbornly high, and the slump in natural diamond prices has hit state finances hard.
situation: In October 2024 voters ended 58 years of Botswana Democratic Party rule, and Duma Boko of the Umbrella for Democratic Change became president. He inherited a recession driven by collapsing diamond sales as lab-grown stones undercut the market. In 2026 his government finalised a new ten-year deal with De Beers giving Botswana a bigger share of the gems, and Debswana planned to raise output by a fifth as demand showed signs of recovering, though the government ruled out reckless spending to prop up the partnership.
power: A parliamentary republic with an executive presidency: the National Assembly elects the president, who heads the government, for up to two five-year terms. A House of Chiefs advises on customary matters.

story: Three Tswana chiefs travelled to London in 1895 to keep their land out of Cecil Rhodes's hands, and Britain ruled it lightly as the Bechuanaland Protectorate. At independence in 1966 it was one of the poorest countries on Earth. Then diamonds were found, and a deal with De Beers and careful management turned it into a middle-income democracy. The Botswana Democratic Party ruled for 58 years until voters threw it out in 2024.
